trajectory_summary: This call moves from a customer-led information request into a clean, procedurally solid booking. The rep correctly resists over-explaining PPA/financing mechanics and holds the in-person-appointment policy under direct pushback, but leaves the customer's spouse-availability problem and financing-structure question open rather than resolved, and the appointment is booked without the wife confirmed on it.

observed_outcome.quote: I'd probably, five ish. Yeah. Five ish would work. Five would work?
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Tuesday) and time (5PM) are locked and confirmed by the customer, and the rep reiterates it at close (10:13). The wife, identified as co-title-holder at 04:23, is never confirmed as attending, and the customer's own comment about both spouses being hard to schedule together goes unresolved.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: Yeah. So last month, which is the bill I just got right now, we used $11.12 for the kilowatt hours.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep collects three months of kWh figures methodically (05:23-06:21) but treats it purely as data-gathering for the design; he never reflects the number or the delivery-fee frustration back as the customer's reason to move forward. The flip should have landed around 06:24 right after the numbers were confirmed, tying the usage data back to the delivery-fee complaint from 02:56.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Well, I've been trying to make my home as energy efficient as possible, over the last year or so, and I've been looking at solar.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asks the interest question early and gets a clear efficiency-motivated answer, but never ties the appointment or design framing back to 'energy efficiency' at button-up — the close is purely logistical (day/time) with no reinforcement of the customer's stated motivation.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: co-owner identified, never confirmed for the appointment
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yeah. It'll be my wife too.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The wife is named as co-title-holder, and the customer separately explains their schedules make it hard to get both of them home together — a direct, spoken barrier to the appointment holding. The rep locks Tuesday 5PM without ever circling back to ask if she'll be there, leaving a structurally fragile booking that the schema flags explicitly (protocols.spouse_decision) as a common setter failure mode.

key_moments.quote: We do both. So we have multiple different options, depending on what what's gonna be the best fit for you or what you, what you prefer.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a soft version of scope creep — the rep answers a financing-mechanism question with a vague generality rather than either a concrete fact or a clean redirect to the specialist. It's not wrong content, but it's also not the universal escape hatch language the schema recommends.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. I'm not quite too sure about all the specifics on on on what works with either one, because, again, my job is just kinda get this design built out, and then, we'll have someone we would get to kinda go over that in a little bit more detail.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the 'admit and recover with transparency' variant of knowledge-gap handling — the rep openly says he doesn't know the PPA-vs-loan differences and correctly routes it to the specialist. This is the right move, arriving one exchange later than it should have.

key_moments.quote: So what got what got me, what caught my attention under your ad is, it says solar, no cost, and you get a, Tesla Powerwall, and stuff like that.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers unprompted interest in the Powerwall battery specifically — a cross-sell-adjacent signal the rep could anchor on. Rep files it into notes but never reflects it back as a hook for the appointment.

key_moments.quote: My energy bill is not very large, but the delivery fees are the ones that are, you know, a little bit upsetting.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a textbook villain-reframe opportunity — he's already frustrated at a specific cost component. The rep never flips this into 'that delivery fee is exactly what solar takes off the table' language; the moment passes into general bill-collection instead.
